Kai Chen: Uploaded an nsys trace from a noisy production repro. Seeing repeated H2D memcpy bursts that line up with CPU scheduling gaps and delayed kernel launches. Suspect KV-cache prefetch path is doing lots of small host copies and serializing the compute stream.

Command I used: 
```bash
nsys profile --output=run_kv_prefetch --trace=cuda,osrt -t cuda,osrt -f true --sample=none --stop-on-duration 60
```

Hand-summarized timeline: 
- stream 7: cudaMemcpy H2D ~12ms (many small chunks)
- stream 0: my_infer_kernel_int8 queued ~14ms after memcpy, runs ~1.2ms
- batcher thread (user) shows 2x 8-12ms user-sched gaps overlapping the memcpy windows

Anyone seen this specific pattern (memcpy -> cpu gap -> delayed kernel)? Could be pinned pool exhaustion or prefetch on the submit thread blocking.

Maya Patel: Are you using cudaMemcpyAsync + pinned pool or falling back to blocking copies? Also can you paste nvtx ranges (kernel selection) — curious if we have a kernel selection stall before launch.

Ravi Singh: Seen similar before. When prefetch chunk size is tiny (<=64KB) we get lots of host->device ops and the copy engine becomes the bottleneck. Increasing chunk size (1-4MB) reduced call frequency and smoothed the timeline. Also try moving prefetch copies to a lower-priority/independent stream.

Kai Chen: Current code does prefetch on the batcher submit path using pinned pages but we sometimes hit a fallback to host memcpy when the pinned pool is exhausted. Small perf snippet from the trace: 
```text
[0.000s] stream 7 memcpy H2D (12.1ms)
[0.012s] stream 0 kernel queued (waited 14.3ms) -> runs (1.2ms)
[0.026s] CPU: batcher thread user-sched gap 10.4ms
```
This looks like: submit thread triggers prefetch, memcpy happens on copy stream but submission of kernel is delayed until memcpy completes (stream ordering), while the batcher thread yields.

perf-bot: Automated check: repeated host->device memcpy observed on same copy stream; >30% of compute time spent waiting for memcpy to finish before kernel enqueue. Recommendations: enable async copies with cudaMemcpyAsync, ensure pinned allocation pool sizing, or route prefetch to a dedicated non-blocking copy stream.

Alex Morgan: Quick experiment: create a dedicated copy stream with cudaStreamNonBlocking and issue cudaMemcpyAsync there. Then on the compute stream call cudaStreamWaitEvent(copy_stream, evt) right before kernel launch. That decouples the copy submission from compute submission and should reduce batching thread stalls. Also consider setting stream priorities so copies don't preempt small latency kernels.

Maya Patel: Another angle: kernel selection path can add latency if we are switching variants based on sequence length at runtime. Set REDWOOD_TRACE_KERNEL_SELECTION=1 to get selection logs — I recall a case where we fell back to a generic kernel which had extra setup cost and increased enqueue-to-start time.

Kai Chen: I'll run two experiments tonight: 1) increase prefetch chunk to 2MB+; 2) route prefetch to dedicated non-blocking copy stream + cudaMemcpyAsync with pinned memory; 3) enable kernel selection logging. Will post new nsys capture after. Thanks for the tips :thumbsup:

Ravi Singh: If the repro persists on dedicated infra ping me and I'll capture perfetto and a longer nsys window (60s might hide low-frequency preemption).
